sources.entry: Speed Test by OpenSpeedTest™ - HTML5 Network Performance Estimation Tool. (Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: A free, open-source, browser-based network speed test written in vanilla JavaScript that runs on any static web server and can be self-hosted, including via Docker.
summary.what_it_does: SpeedTest by OpenSpeedTest is an HTML5 network performance estimation tool that measures download, upload and ping from a web browser using only built-in web APIs (XMLHttpRequest, HTML, CSS, JS, SVG), with no third-party libraries and no client-side software. It consists of static files served by a web server such as NGINX, Apache, IIS or Express, so you can host your own speed test server on a LAN, WAN or cloud machine. It can be run from a Docker image (nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged based), with optional Let's Encrypt SSL or your own certificate. URL parameters control behavior such as stress tests of set duration, automatic test start, parallel connection count, ping sample count, ping timeout, overhead compensation, and choosing a server; the index.html file can be edited to list multiple servers (lowest latency chosen automatically) and to save results to a database endpoint.
use_cases: Test internet speed against a server I host
Check local network throughput between devices
Troubleshoot slow connections or VLAN/switch problems
Compare ISP connections against my own home or office server
Run a continuous stress test of bandwidth
Self-host a speed test on a NAS or home lab with Docker
how_to_run: Or use docker-compose.yml with image openspeedtest/latest and ports 3000:3000 and 3001:3001
Open the browser to the server's HTTP (port 3000) or HTTPS (port 3001) address
For custom deployments, copy the static source files to a web server such as NGINX and follow the provided Nginx config
Optional: enable Let's Encrypt with -e ENABLE_LETSENCRYPT=True -e DOMAIN_NAME=... -e USER_EMAIL=... and ports 80:3000 and 443:3001
notable: No third-party JavaScript frameworks or libraries; script under 8kB gzip
Runs as purely static files, so there are no server-side application security updates to manage
Stress test mode with presets from 5 minutes to a year, or a custom number of seconds
URL parameters for auto-start, parallel connections, ping samples, timeouts and server selection
Works in any browser IE10 or newer
caveats: Browser-based test, so results include unknown overheads; the README says a default 4% overhead compensation is within margin of error
README notes that Docker on macOS or Windows may perform poorly and is intended for development there; Linux is recommended for production
Windows NGINX uses only one worker process, limiting performance
Server must meet requirements such as a 35 MB client_max_body_size and timeouts over 60 seconds
